inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: The agent is instructed to deploy or migrate any named service or database in production on request, using the engineer's own credentials, and is explicitly told never to ask for confirmation. There is no stated limit on what can be named, how often, or when an irreversible action should pause for review.

elements.name: Chat request from engineer to deploy assistant

controls.name: Cloud provider audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Independent of model capability because it is enforced by the cloud platform, but it records actions under the engineer's identity only, not a distinct agent identity, so it does not establish non-repudiation for agent-initiated versus human-initiated actions.

controls.name: Chat transcript as informal request record
controls.decay_rationale: Stored outside the model, but deletable by the same engineer whose request it would need to attest to, so it provides no protection against repudiation once deleted.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval before irreversible production migration
Distinct service identity for agent actions

findings.title: No attributable, tamper-evident record separates agent-initiated production actions from the engineer's own actions

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token, passed in at session start. Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name -- the agent has no distinct identity in the record.

The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript. Engineers can delete their own chat history -- the one record that could show agent-specific intent is destructible by the same person the record would need to hold accountable.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so a misattributed or mistaken action on this path cannot be undone.
"Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy." -- removes the one remaining check that could catch a mistaken or unintended irreversible request before execution.

recommendations.action: Record agent actions under a distinct, non-deletable agent service identity (not the engineer's personal token), in a write-once log, so each production action is attributable to 'agent acting for engineer X' rather than indistinguishable from direct human action.
Require a raw-action human approval step, showing the full migration script and target, before any irreversible production database migration executes.
Retain the chat transcript that records what the agent was asked in a security-owned store that the requesting engineer cannot delete.

forecast.watch_signal: A new, non-SSO or automated trigger (ticketing system, chatops bot, pipeline webhook) begins invoking cap.prod_deploy or cap.db_migrate, or the 'no confirmation' instruction is extended to any automated caller.

stride_coverage.rationale: Only SSO-authenticated on-call engineers can reach the assistant, per runtime notes.

No capability or input in this design allows modification of the agent's own configuration, tools, or prompt; the only input is the engineer's chat request, which maps to deploy or migrate actions, not agent reconfiguration.
Audit log records actions under the engineer's identity only; the agent has no distinct attributable identity.

Neither production capability reads or transmits data to a destination outside the company; both act on production infrastructure using the engineer's own credential, and no egress capability is declared.

Each production action requires a new, individually authenticated engineer request; the design describes no autonomous loop, agent spawning, or spend capability that could cause runaway resource consumption.

The agent acts using the requesting engineer's own personal access token (credential_scope user_delegated), so it cannot exceed privileges the engineer already holds; no broader service credential is described.
Engineer identity is established via company SSO before any request reaches the assistant.
The engineer can delete the chat transcript that is the only record of having made a given request.
The request travels over an SSO-authenticated internal chat channel; the design states no outside content reaches this channel and describes no intermediary able to alter requests in transit.
The channel is internal to the company and restricted to authenticated on-call engineers; the design describes no path by which this request flow is exposed to parties outside that group.
The artifacts do not describe any rate limiting, throttling, or volume controls on the chat channel itself, so its resilience to flooding cannot be assessed from the documents provided.
Engineers can delete their own chat history, which is the only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted.
The transcript is scoped to the individual engineer's own session; the design does not describe shared access, export, or an external viewer for this store.
No capability writes unbounded or high-volume data into this store beyond ordinary chat messages; the design describes no resource exhaustion vector here.
This store is the only agent-specific request record and is deletable by the requesting engineer, so it cannot support non-repudiation.
The design states actions are recorded in the cloud audit log but does not state whether that log is append-only or protected from modification within the production cloud account.
Access controls on who can read the cloud audit log are not described in the artifacts provided, so disclosure risk for its contents cannot be assessed.
The artifacts do not describe whether audit logging has guaranteed availability or whether an account holder could disable or throttle it.
The log attributes every production action to the engineer's identity only, so it cannot establish whether the agent, rather than the human, performed or altered a given action.

rating.rationale: The design has no untrusted input today: all requests come from SSO-authenticated on-call engineers, so there is no complete present attack path into cap.prod_deploy or cap.db_migrate. The dominant present risk is a property gap: the agent acts under the engineer's own credential and is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's identity, so no record distinguishes agent-initiated action from direct human action, and the one agent-specific record (the chat transcript) is deletable by that same engineer. Combined with an irreversible migration capability and an explicit instruction to skip confirmation, this yields a high residual property risk with no control that currently restores attribution. If the chat channel is ever connected to an untrusted or automated trigger (data_scope_expansion) or autonomy is increased, the same unattributable, unreviewed path becomes a complete critical attack path to an irreversible production action, which is why the forecast rises to critical even though no single control is currently relied upon to prevent that path.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP config, or IaC was provided; capability scope, including the data sensitivity of the production database and the blast radius of a deployment, is inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on sink classification for cap.prod_deploy and cap.db_migrate is medium.

No information was provided about request volume or session structure, so the recommended approval gate is stated as a target design (raw_action, low volume) rather than an evaluated existing control.
